family.description: Equivalent host-targeting opportunities for gf2 and pinned gf2x 1.3.0 below the native level: both sides built conservative (no RUSTFLAGS; CFLAGS -O2) or tuned (RUSTFLAGS -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3; CFLAGS -O3 -march=x86-64-v3), compared at a dispatched-kernel size (4 words) and a schoolbook-versus-Toom size (256 words) with operand fixtures identical to the native cells of polynomial-multiplication-baselines. Native-level hypotheses belong to that family and are not repeated here. Every cell is a comparator gap with gf2x as candidate, so a speedup below one means gf2 is faster. The survey adopts nothing, adds no gf2x production dependency and changes no gf2 multiplication algorithm.

effect.rationale: This family declares no improvement cell: every cell compares current gf2 with an external comparator and the issue excludes adoption, so no worthwhile-speedup threshold applies.
effect.equivalence_rationale: Within fifteen percent a consumer choosing between the two libraries decides on portability and licensing (gf2x is GPL-3.0-or-later, gf2 is MIT) rather than on speed. The confirmation freezes a pilot-derived measurement resolution strictly below this margin.
effect.material_gap_rationale: A quarter of the runtime is the smallest gap that survives the adapter and conversion costs a consumer pays to reach an external library, so it is the smallest gap that would change an engineering decision about the gf2 path. The confirmation freezes a pilot-derived measurement resolution strictly below this threshold.

complexity_budget.maintenance_rationale: The survey adopts no implementation and adds no gf2x production dependency, so its budget is zero by construction.
